fieldValues.title: Should signed writes live on commits or on records?
fieldValues.thinking_reached: No option chosen. The owner raised signed writes as a possible future element (vignette 0b9b055b). A commit-based check caught a forged author in the test.
fieldValues.tensions:
Options, none chosen:
- A. Commits only. No spec change and git does the work, but history stays behind when a record moves, and our own server saves are unsigned today.
- B. A signature on each record. It travels with the record and lets a mirror prove it is an unaltered copy, but it needs a spec change and a canonical form to sign.
- C. Commits now, records when a moved record's authorship first has to be verified.

Also: in a group where most people only touch files and one agent keeps the record, whose key signs?
fieldValues.unresolved_questions: What would choose: a real case of a record moved between repositories whose author must be verified, and a test of signing through the save path, one commit per person.
fieldValues.next_action: Try option A in a pilot before designing option B.
